section_summary.extract_value: This section compares body appreciation (BAS) between heterosexual and sexual minority women, finding sexual minority women had higher adjusted BAS (adjusted M = 3.77) than heterosexual women (adjusted M = 3.60) in an ANCOVA controlling for age, BMI, sexual relationship status, and education. Sexual minority participants were older (M=29.17 vs 27.17) and had higher BMI (27.56 vs 25.61); BMI was also significantly related to BAS (F(1,724)=46.84, p<.001). No explicit 'Study 1' or multiple studies are mentioned in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: "Sexual minority participants were 2 years older (M=29.17) than heterosexual participants (M=27.17)... Sexual minority participants also reported larger body size, as measured by BMI (M BMI = 27.56) than heterosexual participants (M BMI = 25.61)... Results indicated there was a statistically significant difference in BAS score for sexual orientation while holding age, BMI, sexual relationship status, and education level constant, F(1, 724) = 8.66, p < .001, partial η^2 = .012; BMI was the only other variable significantly related to BAS, F(1, 724) = 46.84, p < .001, partial η^2 = .061."
